seed: Objects of type `target` under action ACTION3 with touching neighbours [reflection] show mixed outcomes: h,pixels,w,y x1, h,pixels,w,x,y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the exact click position relative to the object, when the action is a click. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Single horizontal mirror axis (wall band of 3x3 blocks) + movable block pieces + fixed target sprites; selection shown by 0-filled hole centres.
A1/A2 move the selection x-/+3, A3/A4 move a selected piece y-/+3 (the axis ignores them); A5 cycles axis -> pieces (by min block) -> axis.
Reflections: piece block b -> 2A-b, clipped to the 21-block board. Render wall<target(solid centre)<reflection<piece; hole centres fill only if the cell is empty; re-extract 4-conn comps; wall/piece names ranked by bbox (x,y) together with all 0 cells.
The target A3 hypothesis was a red herring: those outcomes come from targets being covered or uncovered and re-sorted by visible bbox, not from click position. Passes 30/30 with and without hidden state.
Unconfirmed: blocking by pieces/axis row, and the A5 order after the first piece.
